sources.title: Cyclotomic Completions of Polynomial Rings
sources.edition: Publications of the Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences 40 (2004), 1127–1146, publisher version of record; printed page numbering.
readSections: §1, pp.1127–1128: cyclotomic completion, factorial expansion and roots-of-unity values.
§3.1 and opening of §3.2, pp.1130–1132: monic quotients and cofinal chains.
Theorem 5.2 and its proof, pp.1137–1138: Taylor injectivity.
Conjecture 6.1 and §7.1–§7.5, pp.1141–1146: q inverse, modules, non-surjectivity and the rational Chinese remainder decomposition.

targetCoverage.target: Complete rings, finite quotients, projections and coefficient/restriction maps
targetCoverage.acceptance: Compatible classes modulo P_N; P_0=1 gives the zero precision quotient; projections are surjective with the recorded principal kernels. Completion topology and universal property retain the supplier hypotheses.

targetCoverage.target: Normalised factorial expansion and finite-precision ring arithmetic
targetCoverage.acceptance: F_N=sum_{n<N}P_n; q U_N=1−P_N; multiplication of F by q inverse and F squared renormalizes as in the parent node. For Mathlib remainder use the monic associate (−1)^N P_N, not P_N at odd N.

targetCoverage.target: Evaluation, Taylor coefficients, coefficient naturality and p-adic re-expansion
targetCoverage.acceptance: At order d>0, values use N≥d and Taylor coefficients through degree k use N≥d(k+1). F(1)=1, F(−1)=3, F(ω)=5−ω. Equal values at 1 do not force equal Taylor series. P-adic re-expansion requires a complete separated coefficient ring and a topologically nilpotent shift, not formal substitution with an arbitrary nonzero constant.

targetCoverage.target: Classical injectivity and non-surjectivity with exact hypotheses
targetCoverage.acceptance: The Taylor maps at 1 and −1 of the full integral Habiro ring are injective, not surjective. Evaluation uniqueness uses the parent adjacency hypothesis, never arbitrary infinitude. Inverting 2 and rational coefficients give the explicit failure cases below.

targetCoverage.target: Ordinary module completion and the interface to derived completion
targetCoverage.acceptance: M ↦ M[q]^S is exact for coefficient modules M. The derived identification is imported only for Laurent polynomial modules M[q,q^−1]; arbitrary torsion modules belong to HabiroRings HR.2.

The odd-order idempotent over Z[1/2] has the parent representatives modulo P_2 and P_3. The rational element (q−1)e_1 is nonzero with every root value zero. Modulo 2, q^5+q+1 is idempotent modulo P_3 with the specified two CRT components.

coverage.note: The three imported HC.6 nodes in the accepted parent realise all retained classical targets (see imports and targetCoverage). Accepted RS-10, reviewed 2026-09-29, resolves the sole remaining parent coverage item by assigning the arithmetic comparison to HB.6. AUDIT-17 classifies this as a process/interface stage; no new mathematics or planets. Closure concerns HC.6 only, not unresolved HC.4 refinements elsewhere. The generic exports retain their suppliers' recorded boundaries: in particular the parent non-Noetherian Taylor-injectivity gap is not discharged here. The integral acceptance cases use R = Z and Z[ζ], which are Noetherian; the ordinary-versus-derived comparison is an imported HR.2 interface, not a new construction or a proof that HR.2 is closed.

Checked Habiro introduction, Theorem 5.2, Proposition 7.1 and proof of Proposition 7.4(1); GSWZ Example 5.6 (334); OEIS A022493 data/formula. Independently calculated root values at orders 1–6, ten Taylor coefficients at 1, seven at -1, three at a cube root, finite q inverse and normalized multiplication. The positive-order precision statements follow by counting the factors whose exponent is a multiple of d and hold even in a commutative ring; exact vanishing order needs characteristic zero and primitivity. The unit/non-unit and non-Cauchy examples follow from the stated finite quotient maps. The general non-Noetherian issue is unnecessary for the specified integral cases. All corresponding suggested signatures elaborate.

Checked Habiro §7.5 and GSWZ Example 5.7 (338)–(339). Exact division checks establish compatibility, idempotence and the specified CRT components of e2/e3 over Z[1/2], of e1 and t over Q, and of X^5+X+1 modulo 2. Division by the monic associates introduces no odd denominator, so the localization tests hold in the stated ring. The full families are supplied by HC.5 CRT, not inferred from a single representative. Rational coefficients are distinct from HB.6's arithmetic rational-field ring. Polynomial-module exactness justifies reduction modulo 2. All corresponding suggested signatures elaborate.
